title: Input Symbol Simulation Run
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, and let $x$, $y$, and $r$ be finite Boolean words such that $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$ and $r$. For a register record $R$, suppose every register is at most $B=(8W(N)+8)(|y|+1)$, its position register is at most $|x|+1$, its $N_1$ register equals $|x|+1$, and its $T$, $Z$, $Q_3$, and $Q_4$ registers are zero. Then some $u\le B$ exists such that the step-mode program, starting at label $\mathrm{inZ}$ with register values given by $R$, reaches label $\mathrm{clrQ1v}$ with values obtained by replacing $Z$ by the code of the input symbol at position $R.\mathrm{Pos}$ in $x$, $U$ by $u$, and $Q_3,Q_4$ by $R.A,R.B$; throughout the run, the program's safety condition holds and every register remains at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$y$ is the pair encoding of $x$ and $r$
Every register of $R$ is at most $(8W(N)+8)(|y|+1)$
The position register of $R$ is at most $|x|+1$
